annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "bottle" on page 413 ("Shaun the Post (First Watch)"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within Shaun floating down the Liffey in a barrel, delivering his sermon, the well-fed postman who delivers messages he cannot understand. During this Age of Men phase, they judge, condemn, and demand another round — the Greek chorus of middle-class Dublin gossip.

annotations.annotation_text: Issy/daughter figure "Pepette" on page 413 ("Shaun the Post (First Watch)"): the narcissistic mirror-daughter, modeled on Isolde and Swift's dual muses Stella and Vanessa, appears here within Shaun floating down the Liffey in a barrel, delivering his sermon, the well-fed postman who delivers messages he cannot understand. Her prismatic splitting into twenty-eight Rainbow Girls reflects the cycle's Age of Men phase through youthful seduction and self-reflection.

annotations.annotation_text: Fraternal archetype "Shaun" on page 413 ("Shaun the Post (First Watch)"): the opposing sons — Shem the Penman (introvert artist, tree, darkness) and Shaun the Post (extrovert politician, stone, light) — manifest here within Shaun floating down the Liffey in a barrel, delivering his sermon, the well-fed postman who delivers messages he cannot understand. Their Brunonian dialectic of coinciding opposites propels the chapter's conflict during this Age of Men phase.
sources: Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
